John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Nihonium?
Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
What is the atomic number of Strontium?
Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
In what year did Edward Teller die?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was Oxygen discovered?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
Potassium chloride: Pfizer. Potassium chloride (KCl, or potassium salt) is a metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet E2 family based?
Embraer E-Jet E2 family: Brazil. The Embraer E-Jet E2 family is a series of four-abreast narrow-body regional jet airliners designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer.
Who is credited with discovering Molybdenum?
Molybdenum: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
Who is credited with discovering Serotonin?
Serotonin: Arda Green. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
Who is credited with discovering Beryllium?
Beryllium: Louis Nicolas Vauquelin. Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
Stretching from the thoracic diaphragm to the pelvic brim, this body region sits between the chest and the pelvis — which body part?
Abdomen (also belly or stomach in vertebrates, or metasoma in arthropods) is the front part of the torso between the thorax (chest) and pelvis in humans and in other vertebrates.
This English academic and broadcaster, an anatomist and archaeologist by training, was president of the charity Humanists UK from 2019 to 2022 — who is she?
Alice Roberts (born 19 May 1973) is an English academic, anatomist, archaeologist, TV presenter and author.
This symptom, not a diagnosis by itself, refers to a loss of appetite in humans and — under the name 'inappetence' — in animals from dogs to goats. Which symptom?
Anorexia (symptom) is a medical term for a loss of appetite.
Doctors reach for this NSAID not just for aches but to treat Kawasaki disease and rheumatic fever — and it's famous for its blood-thinning effect on platelets. What is it?
Aspirin is the genericized trademark for acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation, and as an antithrombotic.
Designed to replace the aging Tu-126 'Moss,' this Soviet early-warning aircraft saw only about 42 built before the USSR's breakup ended production in 1992 — what is it?
Beriev A-50 (NATO reporting name: Mainstay) is a Soviet-origin airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft that is based on the Ilyushin Il-76 transport plane.
Caused by a toxin that thrives in low-oxygen conditions — the same one sold cosmetically as 'botox' — this rare illness brings blurred vision and creeping paralysis but rarely a fever. What is it?
Botulism is a rare and potentially fatal illness caused by botulinum toxin (commonly referred to as botox), which is produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.

First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with helium-4 ions, this synthetic actinide element carries atomic number 98, symbol Cf, and the second-highest atomic mass of any element — which element?
Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Discovered in 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi and initially hailed as a new planet, this object in the main asteroid belt is now the only recognized dwarf planet orbiting within Neptune's path — what is it?
Ceres (dwarf planet) is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
What's the statistical term for the extent to which two variables are linearly related — famously not the same thing as causation?
Correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Specialists in this branch of medicine handle skin infections, cancers, hair loss, and cosmetic concerns, sometimes even life-threatening conditions like severe burns — which medical field?
Dermatology is the branch of medicine dealing with the skin.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.
Comprising around 50 species mostly found in the tropics, this fungal genus infects rye, wheat, barley, and other grasses, producing toxic alkaloids — name the group of fungi?
Ergot is a group of fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).
This plant genus of roughly 850 species includes woody trees, vines, and epiphytes native to the tropics, though only two species are widely cultivated for their sweet fruit — what genus is it?
Ficus (or) is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.
This scholarly discipline covers the link between food and culture, from recipes and regional cooking styles to the rigorous science of good eating — what's it called?

Gastronomy is the study of the relationship between food and culture, the art of preparing and serving rich or delicate and appetizing food, the cooking styles of particular regions, and the science of good eating.
Flown by both the U.S. Navy and Britain's Royal Navy under the name Martlet, this 1940 carrier fighter went toe-to-toe with the Mitsubishi Zero over the Pacific — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat is an American carrier-based fighter aircraft that entered service in 1940 with the United States Navy and the British Royal Navy.

Named from the Greek for 'different wings' because most species have forewings that are part membrane, part hardened shell, this group of 40,000 insect species is the one most consistently called 'true bugs' — name this insect group?
Heteroptera are a group of about 40,000 species of insects in the order Hemiptera.
Marked by shivering and confusion in mild cases and hallucinations or paradoxical undressing in severe cases, this condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35°C (95°F) — name it?
Hypothermia is defined as a body core temperature below 35.0 C (95.0 F) in humans.

Once found as far north as Texas's Lower Rio Grande Valley but now extirpated from the US, this slender wild cat comes in gray and red color morphs, ranging from Mexico to Argentina — what animal is it?
Jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi); or is a wild cat native to the Americas.
Endemic to New Caledonia's mountain forests, this bluish-grey, nearly flightless bird sports bright red legs and unique nasal corns shared by no other bird — what is it?
Kagu (Rhynochetos jubatus) is a crested, long-legged, and bluish-grey bird endemic to the dense mountain forests of New Caledonia.
Caused by a specific type of waterborne bacteria, this form of atypical pneumonia brings cough, fever, muscle pain, and headache within days of exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.
Named for antennae often longer than its own body, this insect family boasts over 35,000 species and gets its name from a Greek myth about a shepherd transformed after angering nymphs — which group?
Longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species described.
This computer scientist led the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo Guidance Computer and is credited with coining the very term 'software engineering' — who is she?
Margaret Hamilton (software engineer) (ne Heafield; born August 17, 1936) is an American computer scientist.
This hedge fund manager and licensed physician was among the first to predict and profit from the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, later portrayed on screen in The Big Short. Who is he?
Michael Burry (born June 19, 1971) is an American investor, hedge fund manager, and licensed physician.
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this contractile tissue comes in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth forms and relies on the proteins actin and myosin to generate movement — name the tissue?
Muscle is a specialised soft tissue, one of the four basic types of animal tissues.
Once confused with its chemical twin tantalum, this element with atomic number 41 resists corrosion so well it's used in earrings for people allergic to nickel — which element?
Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
Known for causing bones that fracture easily, this group of genetic disorders can also produce blue-tinted eye whites, short stature, and hearing loss. Name the condition?
Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), colloquially known as brittle bone disease, is a group of genetic disorders that all result in bones that break easily.
Favored by royalty in the Chinese Imperial court, this toy dog breed originated in China's ancient capital — name the breed?
Pekingese (also spelled Pekinese) is a breed of toy dog, originating in China.

A perennial legume native to the Eastern Hemisphere, this crop is a staple across the Indian Subcontinent, Africa and the Caribbean despite a name that sounds more like a bird than a bean. What is it?
Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.

Native to North American grasslands, these burrowing, herbivorous ground squirrels come in five species, black-tailed, white-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah, and Mexican. Name this genus, Cynomys, by its common two-word name?
Prairie dog (genus Cynomys) are herbivorous burrowing ground squirrels native to the grasslands of North America.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).

Nicknamed 'Il Professore' for his academic background, this Italian politician served as European Commission President from 1999 to 2004 and was twice his country's prime minister, first after leading The Olive Tree coalition to victory — who is he?

Romano Prodi (born 9 August 1939) is an Italian politician who served as President of the European Commission from 1999 to 2004 and twice as Prime Minister of Italy, from 1996 to 1998, and again from 2006 to 2008.

These colorful predatory marine animals — single polyps usually anchored by their base — are named after a terrestrial flower and, unlike their jellyfish relatives, skip the medusa stage entirely; what are they?
Sea anemone (-) are a group of predatory marine invertebrate animals constituting the order Actiniaria.
Despite the name, this digestive organ is about 6.5 metres long; it's just narrower in diameter than its large counterpart. What organ is it?
Small intestine is an organ in the gastrointestinal tract where most of the absorption of nutrients from food takes place.
Known by his online username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded an airfare search engine before leading the world's seventh most-visited website as CEO — who is he?
Steve Huffman (born 1983 or 1984), also known by his Reddit username spez, is an American web developer and entrepreneur.
Born in 1946, this American serial killer often posed as an authority figure or feigned injury to lure young women to his car before assaulting and murdering them — who was he?
Ted Bundy (n Cowell; November 24, 1946 - January 24, 1989) was an American serial killer who kidnapped, raped and murdered dozens of young women and girls throughout 1974, 1975, and 1978.
A nasty complication of this inflamed-throat illness goes by the wonderfully old-fashioned name 'quinsy,' or peritonsillar abscess — what's the underlying condition?
Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils in the upper part of the throat.
This phenolic aldehyde is the primary component of the vanilla bean's extract — and its synthetic version now flavors more foods than the natural one does. What is it?
Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Neither an insect nor a parasite despite its common name, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few of its kind to have colonized dry land, likely since the late Paleozoic — what is it?
Woodlouse are terrestrial isopods in the suborder Oniscidea.
Formed when acetic acid combines with a base, this ion is also nature's most common building block for biosynthesis — what is it?
Acetate: Salt formed from acetic acid and a base.
Also known as thymol seeds, bishop's weed, or carom, this Apiaceae herb's fruit is often mistaken for lovage seed — what is it?
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Comprising the talocrural, subtalar, and inferior tibiofibular joints, this region where the foot meets the leg enables dorsiflexion and plantarflexion — which body part?
Ankle: Region where the foot and the leg meet. The ankle includes three joints: the ankle joint proper or talocrural joint, the subtalar joint, and the inferior tibiofibular joint.
The fourth-brightest star in the night sky and the brightest in the northern hemisphere, this aging red giant in Boötes has ballooned to 25 times the Sun's size despite sharing its mass — what is it?
Arcturus: Brightest star in the constellation Boötes. It has the Bayer designation α Boötis, which is Latinized to Alpha Boötis and abbreviated Alpha Boo or α Boo.

Despite its name being something of a misnomer, this herding dog breed was developed in California and takes its name from imported collies that arrived alongside sheep from Down Under — what breed is it?
Australian Shepherd: American breed of dog. The Australian Shepherd, also known as the Aussie, is a breed of herding dog from the United States.
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, this deciduous shrub's glossy dark berries are cooked into jams and syrups or fermented into cassis — what is it?
Blackcurrant: Species of flowering plant in the gooseberry family Grossulariaceae.
Named from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart,' this condition means a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes normal in well-conditioned athletes — which condition?
Bradycardia: Heart rate below the normal range.
Common in cancer, heart failure, and other serious illnesses, this syndrome causes muscle wasting that better nutrition alone can't reverse — what is it?
In 1886 this German engineer patented what's considered the first practical automobile, and his Mannheim company later merged with Daimler — who is he?
Carl Benz: German designer and engineer (1844–1929)
Documented anatomically since the time of Hippocrates over 2,000 years ago, this roughly 4-centimeter-long fibromuscular organ connects the vagina to the uterine cavity. What structure is this?
Cervix: Lower part of the uterus in the female reproductive system.
This Dutch scientist discovered Saturn's largest moon and invented the pendulum clock, the most accurate timekeeper for nearly three centuries — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens: Dutch mathematician and physicist (1629–1695)
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
A heart disease involving reduced blood flow to cardiac muscle due to buildup of plaque in heart arteries — the most common cardiovascular disease. What is it?
Coronary artery disease: Reduction of blood flow to the heart. Procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG) may be used in severe disease.
Named after the bladder because it was first found in urine, this amino acid carries a thiol group that lets it forge the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together. Which amino acid is it?
Cysteine: Proteinogenic amino acid. Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HS−CH2−CH(NH2)−COOH.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this is the sole species in its genus and lives in large, non-hierarchical clans with several breeding females — what's this wild canid called?
Dhole: Species of mammal. The dhole ( dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.

Aristotle's Poetics contrasted this performance-based mode with the epic and the lyrical, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning "deed" or "act" — the two-masks symbol marks its split into comedy and tragedy. What is it?
Drama: Artwork intended for performance; formal type of literature.
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.

Modern phylogenetics calls this a paraphyletic group covering nearly every vertebrate except the tetrapods — gill-bearing, limbless-of-digits, and usually cold-blooded. What aquatic animals are these?
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.

Named for the indigo-blue line seen in its spectrum when discovered in 1863, this soft, silvery-white metal with atomic number 49 is used to make the transparent conductive coating on flat-panel displays — what is it?
Indium: Chemical element with atomic number 49 (In)
Before he proposed that the Earth behaves like one self-regulating living system, this English independent scientist built the detector that first revealed CFCs lurking in our atmosphere. Who was he?

An Alberta-born clinical psychologist and University of Toronto professor, he drew huge attention in the late 2010s for his cultural and political views — self-identifying as a classical liberal. Who is he?
Often miscalled a 'bear,' this tailless, fluffy-eared Australian marsupial is actually a close cousin of the wombat — what is it?
Koala: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia.

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.
Based on the L-188 Electra airliner and distinguished by a tail 'stinger' used to magnetically detect submarines, this four-engine turboprop has served the US Navy since the 1960s — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-3 Orion: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft family.
Occurring naturally as the mineral brucite, this poorly soluble white solid neutralizes stomach acid in a well-known antacid — which compound?
Magnesium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Mg(OH)2.
Part of the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family, some species in this plant genus share the common name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?
Also called androgenetic alopecia, this condition driven by male sex hormones and genetics shows up as a receding hairline or a thinning crown in men — what's the common name for it?
Pattern hair loss: Medical condition. Pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is a hair loss condition that primarily affects the top and front of the scalp.
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Caused by HPV and appearing on the sole of the foot with tiny black dots visible on its surface, this painful skin growth is treated with salicylic acid or freezing — what condition is it?
Plantar wart: Medical condition. A plantar wart, also known as a verruca, is a wart occurring on the bottom of the foot or toes.
Diagnosed only when symptoms like bloating, mood swings, and irritability disrupt daily life in the week or two before a period and resolve once it begins — what's this condition called?
Premenstrual syndrome: Emotional and physical symptoms that occur one to two weeks before a menstrual period.
This water-soluble organic compound, made of two fused rings, gives its name to a class that includes DNA's adenine and guanine bases — what is it?
Named for the way light stretches toward longer wavelengths, this phenomenon comes in Doppler, gravitational, and cosmological forms and is measured by the value z — what is it?
Redshift: Change in wavelength of light.
This British economist, who won the 1991 Nobel and spent decades at the University of Chicago Law School, urged the field to study real-world wealth creation in Adam Smith's spirit — who was he?
Ronald Coase: British economist and Nobel laureate (1910–2013)
First known as a portrait painter, this American inventor helped develop a single-wire telegraph system and lent his name to the dot-and-dash code introduced in 1837 — who is he?
Samuel Morse: American inventor and painter (1791–1872)

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)
This big cat of the genus Panthera prowls the alpine zones of Central and South Asia at elevations of 3,000 to 4,500 meters, from the Himalayas to southern Siberia — what is it?
Snow leopard: Species of large felid.

Named after the patron saint of sailors, this luminous blue or violet glow appears around masts, spires, or aircraft during a strong electric field and can warn of an imminent lightning strike — what is this phenomenon called?
St. Elmo's fire: Luminous plasma created in an electric field.
Occurring in our galaxy roughly once every 61 years, though the last confirmed sighting was back in 1604, this luminous stellar explosion can briefly outshine an entire galaxy?
Encompassing everything from the electrical telegraph to modern radio, this field is defined as the transmission of information over distance using electrical or electronic means — what field is it?
Telecommunications: Transmission of information electromagnetically. The physical limitations of metallic media prompted the development of optical fibre.
Also called T4, this hormone produced by the thyroid gland acts as a precursor to the more active T3 and helps regulate metabolism, heart function and bone health — what is it?
Thyroxine: Thyroid hormone. It is the primary form of thyroid hormone found in the blood and acts as a prohormone of the more active thyroid hormone, triiodothyronine (T3).
Named for its three-lobed shape, this extinct marine arthropod left over 22,000 fossilized species behind after roughly 270 million years in ancient oceans. What creature is it?
Trilobite: Class of extinct, Paleozoic arthropods.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial is the type species that lends its name to an entire genus of flowering plants — what is it?
Valerian (herb): Species of flowering plant. Valerian (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Native to South America and first cultivated by the Guaraní people, the steeped leaves of this holly-genus plant produce a caffeinated beverage — what is it?
Yerba mate: South American holly plant. Yerba mate or yerba maté ( YUR-bə MAH-tay), Ilex paraguariensis, is a plant species of the holly genus native to South America.
The symbol for tungsten is W. Tungsten is a chemical element; it has symbol W and atomic number 74.
The symbol for platinum is Pt. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.

Bray Wyatt: Windham Lawrence Rotunda (May 23, 1987 – August 24, 2023), better known by his ring name Bray Wyatt, was an American professional wrestler.
In what year did Heath Ledger die?
Heath Ledger: Heath Andrew Ledger (4 April 1979 – 22 January 2008) was an Australian actor.
In what year was Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania first released?
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: 2023. Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania is a 2023 American superhero film based on Marvel Comics featuring the characters Scott Lang / Ant-Man and Hope Pym / Wasp.
In what year was Hanu-Man first released?
Hanu-Man (also marketed as HanuMan) is a 2024 Indian Telugu-language superhero film written and directed by Prasanth Varma and produced by K.
In what year was Scream VI first released?
Scream VI is a 2023 American slasher film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett, and written by James Vanderbilt and Guy Busick.
In what year was The Kerala Story first released?
